## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). ## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an

runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI

  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`

  listener open and hand it to the code under test.

- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. **Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

1	# DEVDESK-582 : ligne « proxy » dans les Diagnostics (story 2/3 de DEVDESK-581)
2	
3	Décision utilisateur Q1 : le HEAD des Diagnostics reste **direct**. On ne route rien
4	par le proxy ; on dit seulement si un proxy s'applique à la cible, et la conclusion
5	d'un échec TCP direct le mentionne.
6	
7	## Questions bloquantes
8	
9	**QB1. Verdict de la ligne « Proxy » quand un proxy est configuré pour la cible.**
10	La ligne est une observation, pas un objectif atteint ou manqué ; or `Verdict`
11	n'a que OK / WARN / FAIL / N/A / UNKNOWN.
12	
13	| Option | Rendu | Compromis |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| A. `N/A` partout (sauf valeur invalide = WARN) | `Proxy  N/A  Configured for this target: http://proxy:3128` | aucun type nouveau ; mais « N/A » à côté de « Configured » se lit comme « ne s'applique pas », l'inverse du message |
16	| B. `OK` | `Proxy  ✓ OK  Configured…` en vert | aucun type nouveau ; le vert laisse croire que le proxy a été testé, ce qui est faux (aucun paquet n'y est envoyé) |
17	| C. nouveau verdict `Info` (`INFO`) | `Proxy  󰋽 INFO  Configured…`, couleur de texte ordinaire | le seul qui dise vrai ; touche `Verdict` (String, severity, Summarize l'ignore comme N/A), la cellule, le filtre `p`, l'aide et le contrat MCP (`verdict` gagne la valeur `INFO`, ajout compatible). Environ une demi-journée de plus |
18	
19	Recommandation : **C**. L'étape 2 n'existe que si C est retenue ; avec A ou B, sauter
20	l'étape 2 et remplacer `Info` par `NotApplicable` (A) ou `OK` (B) à l'étape 3.
21	
22	**QB2. L'exception de garde `systemEnv.Handshake` (R4, « DEVDESK-581 story 2/3 »).**
23	Q1 ne vise que le HEAD, mais l'exception TLS porte la même échéance. Options :
24	(a) l'étape TLS reste directe, exception `permanent`, même justification que le HEAD
25	(tout le pipeline mesure le chemin direct ; un handshake tunnelisé mesurerait autre chose
26	que le TCP direct juste au-dessus) ; (b) la REDACTEDer par `netproxy.Dialer.DialTLS` dans une
27	autre story (l'échéance devient cette story).
28	Recommandation : **(a)**. L'étape 6 est écrite pour (a) ; avec (b), seule la ligne
29	`Until` de cette exception change.
30	
31	## Exigences non fonctionnelles
32	
33	- Sécurité : aucune partie userinfo, aucun chemin ni requête de l'URL du proxy, et jamais
34	  la valeur brute d'une variable invalide, ni à l'écran, ni dans le pied de page, ni dans
35	  les journaux, ni dans la sortie MCP. Ce qui est affiché vient d'une seule fonction
36	  (`netproxy.Display`), et une valeur invalide n'est désignée que par le **nom** de sa
37	  variable.
38	- Coût : aucune E/S réseau. On lit l'environnement, en microsecondes. Une étape de plus
39	  dans le pipeline (7 au lieu de 6), qui n'attend rien.
40	- Exploitabilité : la ligne de proxy apparaît aussi dans `net_check` (MCP), parce qu'elle
41	  est un `Check` comme les autres.
42	- Compatibilité : `CheckID` `proxy`, `StageID` `proxy` et les `Reason` ci-dessous sont des
43	  identifiants stables, sérialisés par MCP. Choisir les noms une fois pour toutes (point
44	  irréversible).
45	
46	## Décisions de conception
47	
48	1. **Où la ligne s'insère.** C'est une ligne du tableau des résultats Diagnostics, un
49	   `netcheck.Check` nommé `CheckProxy` (titre `Proxy`), produit par une nouvelle étape
50	   `StageProxy`. Elle se place entre `ICMP echo` et `TCP connect`, sans dépendance
51	   (`dependsOn: ""`), donc jamais sautée : la ligne existe même quand le DNS échoue, ce qui
52	   est le cas courant derrière un proxy obligatoire. On ne touche pas au rendu, puisque
53	   `checkColumns` affiche déjà Title, Verdict et Summary en texte brut (Rule 122). Le
54	   détail (`enter`) montre Explain plus les Facts. On n'utilise ni l'en-tête (7 lignes
55	   fixes, Rule 124), ni le pied de page (réservé aux événements et aux états, Rule 128).
56	2. **Choix « aucune ligne » ou « aucun » : une ligne `None`, toujours présente.** Raisons :
57	   `TestEveryStageProducesWhatItDeclares` impose qu'une étape produise le même ensemble de
58	   checks quel que soit le résultat ; le paquet sépare « pas regardé » de « rien trouvé » ;
59	   la sortie MCP garde une liste stable. Verdict `N/A` (grisé), masqué par le filtre `p`,
60	   sans effet sur le verdict global. Ce choix vaut partout (UI et MCP).
61	3. **Résolution par `netproxy`, sans réimplémenter NO_PROXY.** Nouvelle fonction
62	   `netproxy.Describe(u)` : la réponse vient de `netproxy.FromEnvironment`, la fonction que
63	   tous les clients DevDesk utilisent, avec son cache. Pour la classifier, on lit seulement
64	   le nom et la validité de la variable qui s'applique au schéma. Deux constats faits dans
65	   le code source de Go 1.27 (`vendor/golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy`) :
66	   - Go **ignore silencieusement** une valeur de proxy qu'il ne peut pas analyser
67	     (`config.init` jette l'erreur de `parseProxy`). `FromEnvironment` ne peut donc pas
68	     distinguer « invalide » de « aucun ». Il faut un contrôle de validité à nous
69	     (critère 6).
70	   - Go ne REDACTEDe **jamais** par le proxy pour `localhost` ou une adresse de bouclage. Une
71	     réponse `nil` avec une variable valide et posée signifie donc « bouclage » si l'hôte
72	     en est un, sinon « exclu par NO_PROXY ».
73	
74	   Nous déduisons le résultat, sans recalculer NO_PROXY. Un test en sous-processus fixe
75	   cette déduction contre le vrai `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`.
76	   Alternative écartée : `golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy` en dépendance directe. Elle
77	   donnerait des tests purs, mais ajouterait une dépendance (Rule 303) et un second
78	   calcul, de version différente de celle de la bibliothèque standard, à côté du cache
79	   que les clients utilisent vraiment.
80	4. **Les deux schémas.** Le schéma du HEAD dépend du handshake TLS, qui REDACTEDe après. La
81	   ligne évalue donc `https://hôte:port` (HTTPS_PROXY) et `http://hôte:port` (HTTP_PROXY),
82	   et les fusionne selon la priorité Invalid > Proxied > Excluded > Loopback > None. Les
83	   Facts donnent le détail par schéma.
84	5. **Expurgation.** `netproxy.Display(u)` renvoie `scheme://host:port` (port par défaut
85	   selon le schéma : http 80, https 443, socks5/socks5h 1080 ; sinon l'hôte seul). Jamais
86	   de userinfo, de chemin, de requête ni de fragment. `Decision.Proxy` ne contient que
87	   cette chaîne : l'`*url.URL` brut ne sort pas de `netproxy`.
88	6. **Conclusion (critère 5).** `runConnect` lit la ligne Proxy déjà produite. Si un schéma
89	   au moins est `Proxied` et que le dial direct échoue, le résumé et la `Reason` changent,
90	   et le Fact `Proxy` est ajouté. Le texte d'aide dit que le chemin direct a échoué et
91	   qu'un proxy est configuré, sans répéter « injoignable ».
92	
93	## Libellés exacts (anglais US, Rule 129)
94	
95	Ligne `Proxy` (Title `Proxy`), Summary :
96	
97	| Cas (après fusion) | Verdict | Reason | Summary |
98	|---|---|---|---|
99	| aucune variable pour aucun schéma | N/A | `proxy-none` | `None` |
100	| proxy, même valeur pour les deux schémas | Info (QB1) | `proxy-configured` | `Configured for this target: http://proxy.corp:3128` |
101	| proxy pour un seul schéma | Info | `proxy-configured` | `Configured for this target: http://proxy.corp:3128 (https only)` / `(http only)` |
102	| deux proxys différents | Info | `proxy-configured` | `Configured for this target: http://a:3128 (https), http://b:8080 (http)` |
103	| exclu (au moins un schéma, aucun proxifié) | N/A | `proxy-excluded` | `Excluded by NO_PROXY` |
104	| bouclage | N/A | `proxy-loopback` | `Not used for a loopback target` |
105	| valeur invalide (un schéma suffit) | WARN | `proxy-invalid` | `Invalid HTTPS_PROXY value` / `Invalid http_proxy value` / `Invalid HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY values` (nom tel que lu, casse comprise) |
106	
107	Facts de la ligne : `HTTPS` et `HTTP`, chacun parmi `http://proxy.corp:3128 (HTTPS_PROXY)`,
108	`none`, `excluded by NO_PROXY`, `not used for a loopback target`,
109	`invalid value in HTTPS_PROXY`.
110	
111	TCP connect en échec avec proxy (Reason `direct-failed-proxy-configured`) :
112	Summary `Port 443 does not accept direct connections; a proxy is configured for this target`,
113	Fact `Proxy` = `http://proxy.corp:3128`.
114	
115	Textes d'Explain (Means / Do) :
116	
117	- `proxy-none` (N/A, via `explainNotApplicable`) : Means « No proxy variable is set (HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY or their lowercase forms), so clients on this machine connect directly, the same path these checks test. » Do vide.
118	- `proxy-excluded` (N/A) : Means « A proxy variable is set, but NO_PROXY names this target, so clients connect to it directly, the same path these checks test. » Do vide.
119	- `proxy-loopback` (N/A) : Means « Go programs, DevDesk included, never send localhost or a loopback address through a proxy, whatever the variables say. » Do vide.
120	- `proxy-configured` (Info, ligne de `explanations`) : Means « Browsers and most HTTP clients on this machine, DevDesk's included, reach this target through this proxy. These checks do not: they test the direct path, and nothing here was sent to the proxy. » Do vide.
121	- `proxy-invalid` (Warn) : Means « The variable is set but is not a usable proxy URL. Depending on the value, Go programs, DevDesk included, either ignore it and connect directly, or fail every request they send through it; other tools may read it differently. » Do « Set it to scheme://host:port, for example http://proxy.example.com:3128, or unset it. »
122	- TCP `direct-failed-proxy-configured` (Fail) : Means « The direct path to this port is closed, and that is all this run tests. A proxy is configured for this target: behind a mandatory proxy a closed direct path is expected, and it says nothing about whether the target is up. » Do « If this target is meant to be reached through the proxy, check it from a client that uses it, such as an HTTPS monitor in the Status view. If it is meant to be reached directly, add it to NO_PROXY and look for what drops the connection. »
123	
124	Libellé de progression : `stageTitles[StageProxy] = "Reading the proxy settings"`.
125	
126	## Plan d'implémentation
127	
128	### Étape 1 : `netproxy.Describe` et `netproxy.Display` (parallélisable avec l'étape 2)
129	
130	Fichiers : `internal/netproxy/describe.go` (nouveau), `internal/netproxy/describe_test.go`
131	(nouveau).
132	
133	Interfaces :
134	```go
135	type DecisionKind int
136	const (
137	    DecisionNone     DecisionKind = iota // no variable for this URL's scheme
138	    DecisionProxied                      // a proxy carries this URL
139	    DecisionExcluded                     // a valid variable is set; NO_PROXY names the target
140	    DecisionLoopback                     // a valid variable is set; Go never proxies localhost/loopback
141	    DecisionInvalid                      // the variable is set and is not a usable proxy URL
142	)
143	type Decision struct {
144	    Kind     DecisionKind
145	    Variable string // name of the variable read for the scheme (e.g. "HTTPS_PROXY", "https_proxy"); "" for None
146	    Proxy    string // Display(proxy) when Proxied, "" otherwise
147	}
148	func Describe(u *url.URL) Decision                                         // os.Getenv + FromEnvironment
149	func describe(u *url.URL, getenv func(string) string, sel Selector) Decision // pure, tested
150	func Display(proxy *url.URL) string
151	```
152	Règles de `describe` :
153	- La variable dépend du schéma : https lit `HTTPS_PROXY` puis `https_proxy`, http lit
154	  `HTTP_PROXY` puis `http_proxy` (première non vide, comme `getEnvAny`). Un autre schéma
155	  donne `None`.
156	- La validité suit `parseProxy` de Go (`url.Parse`, puis un nouvel essai avec `http://`
157	  devant) **et** exige un `Host` non vide. Sinon le résultat est `Invalid`, calculé
158	  **avant** de consulter `sel`.
159	- `sel(u)` qui renvoie une erreur donne `Invalid` (le texte de l'erreur n'est jamais
160	  repris). Une valeur non nil donne `Proxied`, avec `Display`. Une valeur nil avec un hôte
161	  `localhost` ou de bouclage (`netip`) donne `Loopback`, sinon `Excluded`.
162	
163	Tests (table-driven, avec `getenv` et `sel` simulés) :
164	- `HTTPS_PROXY=REDACTED`, cible `https://example.com:443`, sel → proxy : `Proxied`, `Proxy == "http://proxy:3128"`, `Variable == "HTTPS_PROXY"`.
165	- La même cible en `http://` sans `HTTP_PROXY` : `None`.
166	- `https_proxy` seul (minuscules) : `Variable == "https_proxy"`.
167	- Variable posée et sel → nil, hôte `intranet.example` : `Excluded`. Hôtes `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` : `Loopback`.
168	- `HTTPS_PROXY="REDACTED"`, puis `"proxy.corp:abc"` : `Invalid`, sans appel à `sel` (le sel simulé fait échouer le test s'il est appelé).
169	- `sel` qui renvoie une erreur contenant `u:p` : `Invalid`, et aucun champ de la `Decision` ne contient `u` ni `p`.
170	- `Display` : `REDACTED` donne `http://p:3128` ; `https://p` donne `https://p:443` ; `socks5://p` donne `socks5://p:1080` ; `http://[2001:db8::1]:8080` donne `http://[2001:db8::1]:8080`.
171	- Garde anti-fuite : pour chaque cas, `fmt.Sprintf("%+v", decision)` ne contient ni `s3cretUser` ni `REDACTED` (jetons distinctifs placés dans chaque URL de test).
172	- Sous-processus (même schéma que `TestFromEnvironmentHelper`) : avec le vrai environnement `HTTPS_PROXY=REDACTED` et `NO_PROXY=intranet.test`, `Describe` vaut `Proxied` (`http://proxy.test:3128`) pour `https://other.test:443`, `Excluded` pour `https://intranet.test:443` et pour `https://api.intranet.test:443`, `Loopback` pour `https://localhost:443`. Un second lancement avec `HTTPS_PROXY="http://[::1"` donne `Invalid`.
173	
174	Commande : `go test ./internal/netproxy -run 'Describe|Display'`.
175	Critère de fin : la commande REDACTEDe, et toute la suite `go test ./internal/netproxy` aussi
176	(la garde n'est pas concernée : aucun transport n'est construit).

179

182	`internal/ui/netdiag/header.go` (aide), `internal/mcp/netcheck_tools.go` (jsonschema),
183	`docs/architecture/mcp.md`.

185	- `Info` est ajouté **après** `Fail` dans l'énumération, pour ne pas renuméroter :
186	  `String()` renvoie `"INFO"`, `severity()` renvoie 0. `Summarize` l'ignore comme

188	- `verdictCell` : `theme.IconInfo + " INFO"`. `verdictStyle` : style de texte ordinaire
